lens: Spermidine's conserved role in autophagy induction and polyamine transport kinetics [2,4,6] suggests a unified framework for stress resilience across kingdoms, but divergent dose-response thresholds in reproduction [1] versus agriculture [3] challenge translational extrapolation, necessitating a focus on cellular transport mechanisms as a novel intervention point.
known_to_ignore: Spermidine at 0.5 mmol/L improves boar sperm motility and membrane integrity [1,7]
Spermidine pretreatment increases rice yield in cultivars like KDML105 and Pokkali [3,9]
SAT1 overexpression depletes spermidine and arrests HeLa cell growth [2]
tensions: Between [2] (SAT1-mediated polyamine depletion causes growth arrest in HeLa cells) and [3] (exogenous spermidine at 1 mM enhances rice yield), highlighting context-dependent effects of polyamine levels on growth

In [6], OCT inhibitors block spermidine uptake in boar sperm, but analogous transport mechanisms in plants, such as in lime seedlings [13], remain uncharacterized, creating a gap in understanding cross-kingdom polyamine kinetics

Autophagy blockade with 3-MA in [4] reverses spermidine's benefits in nucleus pulposus cells, while similar autophagy-dependent mechanisms in mouse models [8] are not directly linked to spermidine, indicating mechanistic inconsistency
gaps: No studies on spermidine's role in human seminal plasma preservation, despite boar data [5]
Limited exploration of spermidine's synergistic effects with other phytohormones like brassinolide under stress, as seen in maize [19] but not generalized
Absence of dose-finding studies for oral spermidine supplementation to induce autophagy in humans, bridging in vitro [4] and animal [8] evidence

theses.title: OCT Transporter Inhibition as a Strategy for Modulating Spermidine Flux in Reproductive Biotechnology
theses.rationale: Synthesizes kinetic data from OCT inhibitor studies [6] with functional sperm outcomes [1,5,7] to propose targeted transport-based interventions for cryopreservation, a niche angle beyond mere supplementation.

theses.title: Autophagy-Dependent Spermidine Cytoprotection: From Nucleus Pulposus Cells to Intervertebral Disc Disease Therapeutics
theses.rationale: Focuses on the mechanistic link in [4] to identify a translational gap for degenerative disc disease, leveraging autophagy specificity despite high risk due to limited in vivo data.

theses.title: Quantifying Spermidine Priming Efficacy Across Cereal Crops: A Pilot Meta-Analysis of Dose and Cultivar Variability
theses.rationale: Aggregates heterogeneous agronomic data [3,9,12,13,17,19] to establish dose-response relationships, addressing climate resilience with a publishable quantitative synthesis.

reviewer_objections: The boar sperm model [1,5,6,7] may not extrapolate to humans due to species-specific polyamine metabolism and OCT expression differences
Autophagy blockade in [4] uses 3-MA, which has off-target effects on other pathways, questioning the specificity of spermidine's mechanism
Agronomic studies [3,9,12] vary in spermidine doses (0.1 μM to 5 mM) and application timing, complicating meta-analysis and reducing generalizability
Food content studies [20,21] lack controlled intake trials, making it difficult to link dietary spermidine to health outcomes
next_extractions: Spermidine and polyamine transporter expression profiles in human seminal fluid under assisted reproduction protocols
Spermidine combined with brassinolide (BRs) at 1.0 mmol L−1 in maize cultivar Xingken-6 under extended waterlogging stress beyond 14 days [19]
Histatin 5-spermidine conjugate (Hst 54-15-Spd) efficacy in immunocompromised mouse models with oral candidiasis for preclinical optimization [24,25]
